comparison: Strong agreement on VAF transitions and theoretical predictions (C3, C16, C19, C20, C54, C55). OpenEval notes C21's linear mutation rate increase requires alternative explanation, while peer reviewers affirm the work provides 'clear insight' without challenging this finding. OpenEval includes C21 here while peer review addresses it in R2.

Both address alternative explanations for mutation rate trends (C23, C24, C69-C71). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to speculative biological mechanisms requiring validation, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting the novel observations and mechanistic proposals without challenge.

Perfect agreement on sample size analysis (C4, C27, C28, C59). Both affirm the simulation results showing inference quality plateaus beyond ~100 cells. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the methodological contribution as 'important contribution to the literature.'

Both address elevated mutation rates and competing explanations (C5, C29, C31-C34, C44). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to multiple possible mechanistic explanations requiring additional data, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the estimates without challenging the uncertainty.

Strong agreement on single-cell VAF fitting approach (C6, C36-C41, C65-C67, C80). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical rigor and biological constraints; peer reviewers affirm the methods 'nicely describe and make inferences.' Peer R6 includes C43 and C72 which OpenEval addresses separately.

Perfect agreement on over-dispersion findings and model incompleteness (C7-C10, C35, C46-C49, C68). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the logical chain is sound though mechanisms remain speculative; peer reviewers accept this as providing 'clear insight into when previous theoretical results break down.'

Both address complementary nature of approaches (C42). OpenEval includes C43 and emphasizes integration of bulk and single-cell data; peer reviewers explicitly support this central conclusion, noting the work 'combine single cell and bulk sequencing analyses' to inform different aspects.

Perfect agreement on sampling effects and hypergeometric correction (C62, C64, C76, C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical soundness; peer reviewer explicitly acknowledges 'sub-sampling does increase noise' and validates these findings.

Both address fundamental limitation of mutational burden approach (C72). OpenEval separates this as distinct result; peer review includes it within broader single-cell VAF analysis (R6). Both affirm this limitation is appropriately acknowledged.

Both address background knowledge claims (C1, C2, C11). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED established principles; peer reviewers implicitly accept these foundational statements. Peer R9 includes broader set of literature citations (C12, C22, C25-C26, C45, C74-C75, C79, C81-C82) that OpenEval addresses in R11 and R13.

Both address established knowledge from previous studies (C12, C22, C25-C26, C74-C75, C79, C81-C82). OpenEval separates these from background principles (R10); peer review groups all literature context together. Both rate as SUPPORTED without challenge.

Perfect agreement on mathematical derivation of symmetric vs asymmetric division contributions (C83). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes mathematical soundness; peer reviewers praise 'strong methods' without challenging derivations.

Both address emerging evidence about selection in aging blood (C45). OpenEval separates this as context for model limitations; peer review groups it with other literature citations. Both accept as established context without challenge.
